utility.notes: Iowa City's own solar page directs installers filing interconnection requests to 'the utility's webpage...for MidAmerican customers,' confirming MidAmerican as the relevant utility for at least a substantial share of Iowa City properties. MidAmerican's own consumer website (midamericanenergy.com) was unreachable this session (confirmed blocked earlier in this marathon), so utility-specific interconnection details are instead sourced from the Iowa Utilities Commission's own regulatory record of MidAmerican's filed tariff.

value.name: MidAmerican Energy Company
value.notes: Recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_url.notes: This URL returns HTTP 403 to automated HEAD requests (a bot-detection response, not a broken page); the page's actual content was independently confirmed live and readable via direct browser navigation this session.

interconnection_url.notes: Iowa does not permit traditional full-retail-rate net metering. Iowa Code § 476.49 instead requires MidAmerican Energy and Interstate Power and Light (Alliant Energy) to file net billing or inflow-outflow compensation tariffs with the Iowa Utilities Commission. The IUC's own page confirms MidAmerican's approved tariff is Rate IO (Inflow/Outflow Billing), Docket No. TF-2020-0235, effective November 24, 2020 — under which exported energy is credited as a dollar amount at the outflow purchase rate, applied toward volumetric charges, rather than banked as a 1:1 kWh credit at the full retail rate.

battery_programs.notes: Iowa City's own page confirms battery storage can be permitted alongside a solar array under the same permit process, but no dedicated battery storage financial incentive program was found this session.

value.program_or_pathway: Solar PV is permitted by right as an accessory structure in Iowa City (no special board review required). Grid-tied systems interconnect with MidAmerican Energy under Iowa's net billing/inflow-outflow framework (Iowa Code § 476.49; Iowa Administrative Code 199-45 for interconnection, 199-15 for Cogeneration and Small Power Production Rules) rather than traditional net metering, which Iowa state law does not permit.
other_conditions: Iowa state law does not allow traditional full-retail-rate net metering; MidAmerican Energy's IUC-approved tariff (Rate IO, Docket No. TF-2020-0235, effective 11/24/2020) instead credits exported energy as a dollar amount at the outflow purchase rate.
Iowa law requires the distributed generation system owner to notify their interconnected electric utility at least 30 days before installing a distributed generation system.

Solar arrays are allowed in all Iowa City zoning districts, including Historic and Conservation Districts; a streamlined historic-review process applies when the array is on a rear-facing or outbuilding roof, mounted close to and parallel with the roof surface, and colored to blend with the roofing materials — otherwise a standard Historic Preservation Commission review applies.

Iowa's residential Solar Energy System Tax Credit is no longer available for systems installed in 2022 or later, but Iowa City confirms solar arrays still qualify for a state property tax exemption on the added value for the first five years after installation.
Since January 2023, Iowa City ordinance prevents newly formed HOAs (or new HOA solar rules) from being more restrictive of solar installations than the City's own regulations.

permit_fees.notes: Iowa City's own page lists 'permitting' as one of several cost categories a homeowner should ask installers about, but does not publish a specific dollar figure or fee schedule on the page itself — left null rather than guessed.

rebates.notes: Iowa City's own page explicitly confirms Iowa's residential Solar Energy System Tax Credit is no longer available for systems installed in 2022 or later — a confirmed negative rather than an unresearched gap. No other rebate dollar amount was found this session.
